summary.title: BrainFrame P2P Sync Threat Model
summary.description: BrainFrame is a second brain and archiving program. It provides cross platform support (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iPhone/iPad), and builds in a way to synchronize data amongst a collection of devices. This threat model focuses on the synchronization mechanism

data.name: Peer
data.description: UI Peer, Headless Peer. Can be reading or writing.

data.name: Engram Files
data.description: Markdown, PDF, EPUB. Eventually will include FLAC, WAV, and video formats.

data.name: .brainframe
data.description: engram identity, version information, per engram settings, such as the visual theme, and peer level identity maps

Peer renders documents to keeper.

Peer provides pairing codes to keeper

Keeper sends commands (remove peer, accept quarantined edits)
Keeper confirms pairing with other peers

data.description: All data between the standalone peer and the blind peer hosted by the services passes through this network ingress. First block of any attempted improper access.

data.name: Verification Email Send Request
data.description: BrainFrame requests a verification email be sent to the keeper. This includes a unique link that the keeper clicks to confirm they own this email account. Provisioning requires verified accounts.

data.name:
BrainFrame

data.description: Account recovery, account verification during signup, any news/updates related to the service

data.name:
Infrastructure
Secret Store
data.description: Dangerous for exposure: These secrets will include payment processor API keys. In addition, webhook signing secret, OIDC client secret, email provider key, and website's private TLS key land here. Other (as yet undefined) secrets may also go here. Risks of exposure here will see customers get marked as cancelled and data deleted because of it, as well as complete disablement of the website and other infrastructure. Could result in blind peers becoming inoperable, though that is less likely.

data.name: Usage records
data.description: time based usage logging for a given engram: disk storage and network transfer in/out

text.text:
"Blind Peer N" does not guarantee a single
process per peer. It is expected that this will
be implemented as a single process. This
means that code must enforce multi-tenancy
properly, and not rely on running different
containers/VMs to keep engrams separated
from each other.

data.description: Biggest risk to customers here. This store contains TLS secret keys, and cloud storage keys (allowing a single command to mass-delete *everything*). High risk here, focus time.
